source.tamil_title: வெல்க நாடு வெல்க நாடு வெல்க வெல்கவே

translation.english_title: May the land triumph, may the land triumph — triumph, triumph!

source_tamil_lines: வெல்க நாடு வெல்க நாடு வெல்க வெல்கவே
வீர சங்க நாதம் கேட்டு செல்க செல்கவே
தாயின் ஆணை கேட்பதற்கு தலை வணங்கும் தங்கமே
உன் குன்று தோளில் புது பலத்தை வழங்குமடா நித்தமும் சென்று வா -
மகிமை கொண்ட மண்ணின் மீது எதிரிகளின் கால்கள்
english_lines: May the land triumph, may the land triumph — triumph, triumph!
Hear the warrior-conch blast and go, go!
Let the armies go — let the armies go...
(May the land triumph)
Golden one who bows the head to heed the mother's command,
Give your head and guard the mother's honour, O lion,
Go and return — win and return...
(May the land triumph)
Speaking baby-talk like kumalai,
the kisses of the children,
and the lovely-voiced sound
of coaxing Anjugam,
will give new strength every day to your hill-like shoulder, da — go and return —
win and return...
(May the land triumph)
Upon the glorious soil — the feet of enemies,
the feet of enemies,
Warriors' hands do not pluck flowers, da,
the hands of great warriors,
Go and return — win and return...
(May the land triumph)
His form is like an upraised sword, da — his,
radiant eyes are the mould of the world, da,
He is the vengai-tiger king, da,
the leader of warriors, da — await his,
command, good one,
Set out toward the battlefield, mighty one..
(May the land triumph)
notes: The refrain keeps repeated `வெல்க / செல்க / சென்று வா / வென்று வா` exhortation instead of condensing the marching rhetoric.
`தாய்` remains mother rather than being silently expanded to motherland where the source does not do so.
The verified unusual `குமலைப்` is retained as `kumalai`; the source itself does not justify replacing it with a normalized form.
`அஞ்சுகத்தின்` is conservatively retained as `Anjugam` rather than silently deciding whether the source intends a name or another lexical form.
`குன்று தோள்` remains a hill-like shoulder, and the direct `டா` force is selectively retained as `da`.
The stark line that warriors' hands do not pluck flowers remains literal.
`வேங்கைப் புலி` remains `vengai-tiger`, and the verified source form `புறப்படடா` is not used as a pretext to rewrite the Tamil.

translator_notes: The song's martial language remains source-shaped: conch blast, armies, head-giving, mother's honour, children's kisses, hill-like shoulder, enemy feet, flower-not-plucking warrior hands, raised sword, radiant eyes, tiger-king and battlefield command.
Source pressure points `குமலைப்`, `அஞ்சுகத்தின்`, and `புறப்படடா` are documented rather than normalized through English.
